sections.en: 1 ἱππονεμεύταις ('horse-pasturers') the codex has; corrected; a new word, but ἱππονομεύς ('horse-keeper') and αἰγονομεύς ('goat-keeper') are found: ἱππονομεύταις ('horse-pasturers') was the end of a hexameter. 4 πλ(άτει) ('in breadth') by abbreviation the codex has. Should it be read πόλῳ ('pole')? 6 καταβάταις ('descenders'), τα written above, the codex has. 7 ἀθυμίαις ('despondencies') scarcely sound. 8 σαλπηγηταῖς ('trumpeters') as it seems the codex has. 9-25 Cf. Boll, Sphaera, p. 543 s. 9 Ἑρμαϊκά ('Hermaic')] cf. p. 187, 22. οἱ ('the') supplied by Boll. 16 ἡδυπαθεῖς ('living pleasantly') the codex has. 18 ἱπποδρομίαις ('chariot races') from ἱπποδρόμοις ('hippodromes') corrected, the codex has. 22 μυρλιανὸς ('Myrleanian') the codex has. On the Sphaera barbarica of Asclepiades of Myrlea, cf. Boll, l. c., p. 544 s. Albin. Müller, De Ascl. Myrl., Lipsiae, 1903, p. 22 ss. 30 ματράσι ('mothers') the codex has. 31 ὑγρός ('wet') is a tender boy. ἀπαγελ(οις) ('not in a herd') the codex has: ἀπάγελος ('not in a herd') is a youth born less than XVII years ago (Hesychius). 32 πλησιοσέληνος ('near the moon') the codex has.

1 In epitaphiis Sol saepe invocatur ut eum qui iuvenem dolo malo interfecit,
indicet; cf. notulam meam ad titulum ex Amiso Ponti in Rev. études gr., 1904.
sections.en: 1 In epitaphs the Sun is often invoked so that he might point out him who killed a youth by evil deceit; cf. my short note on the inscription from Amisus in Pontus in Rev. études gr., 1904.

summary.headline: Astrological Correspondences and Planetary Roles
summary.text: Astrological correspondences linking zodiacal signs, constellations, fixed star Spica, decans, and planets with occupations, social roles, rites, and ages. Asclepiades of Myrlea and Hermes Trismegistus are cited as authorities, with the Sun and Moon assigned to kings, fathers, queens, mothers, youths, and elders.
